Hannah —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our renewal is coming up in July and the execs want two things clarified before we sign: (1) a formal plan for EU onshore hosting of PHI-adjacent metadata (we can't have token storage in the US for EU region traffic), and (2) an APAC standby/rollout plan so we can support pilot traffic in Singapore with a fast failover to the EU node.

High level asks:
- Can Redwood provide an EU-dedicated model variant and garantueed node(s) for our EU customers?
- Can we add a warm-standby APAC node that can be promoted to hot within X minutes during failover?
- Pricing impact and any term adjustments for region isolation + standby capacity?

If you can send an SOW addendum and a sketch of the architecture, we can route to procurement this week.

— Emma

Emma — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers at a high level and next steps below.

Short answers:
- Yes: we can offer an EU onshore tenancy (dedicated model runtime + storage partitioning) as an addendum to your renewal.
- Yes: we support an APAC warm-standby (Singapore) that can be configured for automated promotion; SLA for promotion time is a configurable SLO in the SOW.
- Pricing: two parts — a capacity reservation for dedicated EU nodes (commit-based monthly fee) + a standby premium for APAC warm capacity. We can propose a blended per-token uplift or a flat monthly standby charge.

Proposed next steps:
1) Ben and Monica to draft an SOW addendum with options (A: EU dedicated + APAC standby; B: EU dedicated + APAC burst only; C: staggered APAC pilot w/ metered standby).
2) We'll include an estimated cost delta + recommended SLO for failover (30/60/120 min options).
3) I'll loop Legal for a short residency exhibit for the contract redline.

Can we schedule a 30-min call tomorrow to run through the options? I'm available 10:30–12:00 and 15:00–16:30 PT.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Draft SOW addendum: EU onshore + APAC warm-standby (v1)

Team —

Attached is v1 of the SOW addendum for TheraGen. Highlights:
- Architecture: EU dedicated model runtime + encrypted on-disk token/key store in EU KMS; APAC warm-standby runs a scaled-down GPU pool that keeps KV cache primed and can be scaled to full throughput via automated promotion. See attached diagram.
- Failover: three promotion SLO options (30/60/120 minutes). The SOW includes runbook, DR play, and health probes.
- Pricing: EU dedicated node set (3 x A100-equivalent) on a reserved monthly commit; APAC warm standby as a 25% reserved capacity with pay-as-you-go burst top-up. We included sample pricing and the uplift for managed residency compliance.
- Term: 12 month base with option to extend to 24 months at a 7% discount; early termination fees listed for decommissioning dedicated EU capacity.

Notes for Hannah: please confirm which SLO option Emma wants on the call. Also, procurement will ask for evidence for our EU KMS and SOC2 practices — Monica, can you pull the residency checklist and the appropriate redacted audit artifacts?

Thanks,
Ben
Director, Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference

Emma —

Quick answers to your procurement/infra questions below. I'm including the checklist attachment referenced earlier.

1) Per-tenant KMS keys: supported. We can provision a customer key hierarchy inside EU KMS and integrate with your tenant IDs. We'll call this out in the residency exhibit.

2) Promotion cost delta estimates (APAC warm -> hot):
- 12-hour incident window: estimated additional cost = 1.8x of baseline APAC standby monthly charge (covers GPU hours + data egress/priming).
- 72-hour incident window: estimated additional cost = 3.6x baseline (sustained hot utilization). Exact figures depend on traffic profile; we included sample numbers in the spreadsheet.

3) Promotion runbook + audit trail:
- Trigger authority: TheraGen infra lead OR designated Redwood on-call (mutual-auth).
- Promotion steps: health checks -> route switch -> capacity scale -> KV priming -> smoke tests -> cutover confirmation.
- Audit trail: every promotion event emits an immutable incident record (timestamp, actor, pre/post capacity, logs) stored in the customer's EU audit bucket for 7 years (or per your retention policy).

If that matches what procurement expects, we'll bake these specifics into SOW v2 and circulate redlines. Hannah — want to propose a redline session time Wednesday morning?

Regards,
Monica Patel
Director, Product Compliance, Redwood Inference
